mainEntity.name: How much does a Mazda 6 petrol engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Mazda 6 petrol (LF17, L5-VE) engine replacement typically costs between £750 and £2,200 for the engine supply alone, depending on whether you choose used, reconditioned, or rebuilt. Supply and fit adds approximately £390-£520 in specialist labour. Dealer pricing can add 30-50% to these figures.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the Mazda 6 petrol engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: MZR petrol engines (LF17, L5-VE) are generally reliable but have three well-documented issues. Coil pack failure causes hesitation and misfires. VVT actuator wear causes cold-start rattle. Timing chain stretch on high-mileage units can occur if VVT issues are ignored.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mazda 6 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on the vehicle's value and condition. A typical older Mazda 6 petrol is worth £1,000-£4,000. A rebuilt engine at £1,500-£2,200 may represent a significant portion of the vehicle's value. If the car is in good condition, well-maintained, and you intend to keep it for 2+ years, replacement is often worthwhile. If vehicle value is under £1,500, evaluate scrap value first.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the GG and GH generation engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The GG (2002-2007) and GH (2007-2013) generation petrol engines share the same MZR engine family. The LF17 2.0L and L5-VE 2.5L engines were used across both generations with minor revisions. The GH generation also introduced the 2.5L L5-VE and 1.8L L813.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between LF17, L5-VE, and LF-DE engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: LF17 is the 2.0-litre MZR petrol engine (141-147hp) used in GG and GH generations. L5-VE is the 2.5-litre MZR petrol engine (170hp) used in GH generation. LF-DE is the 2.0-litre MZR petrol (155hp) used in late GH production (2010-2013) with revised mapping.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mazda 6 petrol engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional Mazda 6 petrol engine replacement typically takes 1-3 working days. Specialist workshops can complete the job in 6-8 labour hours. Supply lead times vary: used engines 2-5 working days, reconditioned 5-10 working days, and rebuilt 7-14 working days. Confirm exact timelines with your chosen specialist.

historyTimeline.h2: Mazda 6 Petrol (GG/GH) - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mazda 6 petrol engines across the first-generation GG (2002-2007) and second-generation GH (2007-2013) platforms used the MZR engine family, offering 1.8L, 2.0L, and 2.5L naturally aspirated petrol units. These engines are known for their robust design and widespread parts availability .

milestones.description: GG generation launched; 2.0L MZR LF17 introduced (141-147hp) with DOHC 16V and timing chain
2008 - GG generation engines across hatchback, saloon, and estate body styles
MPS performance variant launched with 2.3L DISI Turbo (260hp)
GH generation launched; 2.0L MZR LF17 continued alongside new 2.5L L5-VE (170hp)
2013 - GH generation engines across all body styles; 1.8L L813 (120hp) also available
End of GH production; third-generation GJ introduced with Skyactiv-G engines

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mazda 6 petrol (GG and GH generations) is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Mazda 6 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mazda 6 petrol MZR engines are generally reliable, but like any high-mileage unit, they have well-documented issues. Coil pack failure, VVT actuator wear, and timing chain stretch are the primary drivers of replacement demand. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.
